current_answer: The EIC Accelerator 2026 is open to suitable deep-tech startups and SMEs in EU Member States and eligible Horizon Europe-associated countries. The grant component is below EUR 2.5 million for TRL 6–8 work, but a 4 November full-proposal slot requires a prior GO on a short proposal. That first stage alone asks for a 12-page form, a deck, and a video, with feedback normally in 4–6 weeks. A new applicant should not treat 4 November as a one-step deadline or the grant ceiling as an award.

catalogue_card.question: EIC’s 4 November grant batch is not your first application step.
catalogue_card.text: A full proposal needs a GO on an earlier short proposal. That first stage needs 12 pages, a deck and a video; EIC says feedback normally takes 4–6 weeks. The grant component is below EUR 2.5 million for suitable TRL 6–8 work, not a promised award.

summary: EIC short proposals can be submitted at any time; full proposals need a GO before the next 4 November 2026 batch at 17:00 Brussels time.
The grant component is below EUR 2.5 million for TRL 6–8 innovation work; the investment component is separate, not grant cash.
The short stage needs a 12-page form, up-to-10-slide deck, and up-to-three-minute team video. Feedback normally takes 4–6 weeks.
A 4 November full proposal then needs a 20-page form and supporting financial, implementation, freedom-to-operate, and intent materials.
uncertainty: A fresh short proposal may not clear review before the 4 November full-proposal batch.
Country-specific eligibility, especially grant versus investment access, needs a current issuer check; the main page and FAQ differ on the UK.
